chapter: Cass Carr, Crawley, Burnet and Cootie Williams
title: Cass Carr's gigging band, his bass and musical saw
summary: Cass Carr led ten-piece gig bands with a bass violin and a saw, used many New York musicians, paid reliably and later became a photographic-equipment seller.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I see!
[LAUGHS] You know, it was a novelty. But
Holmes (11/29) - 2

he was quite a bandleader. He would get a lot of work. Just gig work. He didn't work anywhere steady or anything like that. He was just giggin'. And he had a nucleus to his band, which I don't remember... But he would always have openings for anybody that was giggin'. And that way, he used, oh, numerous musicians that was in the street giggin', lookin' for gigs and one-thing-or-another. They could always get a gig with Cass Carr. That's that they called him. He shortened his name from Casper Cowie(?) to Cass Carr.
Oh, it was Cowie(?), not Towey(?).

Well, I don't know what it was. But they called him Cass Carr. And he survived for years in the business. And he was a very good photographer. He went in for photography more than he was music. He was interested in taking pictures, and one-thing-or-another. And now, he's in the line of... He sells photographic instruments. He sells photographic instruments to professionals. He's got a place downtown somewhere. He's out of the music business altogether.
But you gigged with him, though.
Oh, plenty of times. Numerous times, yes.
What type of groups were they? Five or six pieces?
No. He had ten pieces, up... What the
Holmes (11/29) - 3
occasion called for. But he would always have three saxophones at least, three brass at least -- and more sometimes.
What kind of work, then? Society work? What kind of gigs did he get?

Well, I wouldn't call them Society. It was dances. He played for different groups in clubs and things. Dance music. But he had some good musicians in the band. You know Bob Williams. He worked with him many a time.
I see.
Oh yeah. In fact, anybody you name, they have worked with Cass Carr. Any of the musicians that you know, they have worked with Cass Carr.
When he had his bands together, did he primarily then play his guitar?
Well, no. He primarily played bass violin. He played bass violin. And then he would draw his saw out in the middle of the night...! Which was nice. He had a number that he did on the saw, you know.
Do you remember the number?
No. Who would want to remember it? But I mean, it was his band. He'd play what he'd want to play! And I mean, if you didn't react to the way he thought you should... No, strike that out.
Holmes (11/29) - 4
You were out of his band!
You were out of the band.
Well, who were some of the other saxophonists that you...?
Well, at different times, I mean, he had... He's had them all. Howard Johnson and... You name them, he's had them. It's a funny thing.
And he paid off all right, right after the gig, or did you have to wait...?

Oh yeah, you got paid. Yeah. He didn't mess with your money. He might be a little light on it. I mean, he might not pay as much as everybody else, or one of them things. But he didn't mess with your money. You didn't have to worry about it.
So in other words, if he called you for a gig, you'd take it.
Yeah, you'd get your money.
